claims.claim: A list comprehension creates a new list using bracketed syntax containing an expression and at least one for clause.
A list comprehension may include zero or more if clauses that filter candidate values before the expression contributes an element.
The for and if clauses in a comprehension correspond in left-to-right nesting order to an explicit loop-and-condition version.
In Python 3, a comprehension executes in an implicitly nested scope except for the leftmost iterable expression, so its target name does not leak into the enclosing scope.
A simple one-line transformation or filter can be clear as a comprehension, while several clauses or substantial branching are often clearer as an explicit loop.
